ruleName: Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions (Including Immovable Obstructions)
title: Ball moving in temporary water: must the player lift it immediately?
question: Peter’s ball is moving in temporary water and he intends to take relief. Must Peter immediately lift the moving ball?

choices.text: No. He may allow it to move to a better position before taking relief, provided he does not unreasonably delay play.
Yes, unless another player agrees otherwise.

explanation: A player whose ball is moving in temporary water may allow it to come to rest in a better position before taking relief, provided that they do not unreasonably delay play. There is no requirement to lift the ball immediately.

juniorVersion.title: Ball floating in a puddle: Do you have to pick it up right away?
juniorVersion.question: Peter’s ball is slowly floating in a puddle, and he wants to move it because of the water. Does Peter need to pick up the ball straight away?

choices.text: No. He can wait and let the ball stop in a better spot, as long as he doesn’t take too long.
Yes, unless another player says it’s okay to wait.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball is moving on its own in a puddle, you can wait for it to stop in a nicer place before picking it up. Just don’t wait too long, so you don't slow down the game.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Moving your ball to a better place when something like water or a big thing is in your way.
A puddle of water on the course that shouldn’t be there all the time, like after rain.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Act out a ball moving in a puddle and talk about when to pick it up and when it’s okay to wait.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think you must pick up the ball right away, but you can wait if it’s not slowing down play.
Kids may think you need another player to say it’s okay to wait, but you don’t.
